tutor.message: Condensation happens when warm water vapor in the air cools down and turns back into liquid water droplets!
tutor.why_prompt: Where have you noticed water droplets forming in everyday life, like on a cold glass on a hot day?
explanation_steps: Water exists in the air as an invisible gas called water vapor.
When the water vapor cools down, it changes physical state.
The vapor turns back into tiny liquid water droplets, forming condensation.

review.note: The direction is correct. Warm air, cooling, invisibility and the cold-glass example go beyond the one-sentence source. The follow-up asks for an everyday observation.

tutor.message: Not quite! Evaporation actually goes in the opposite direction, changing liquid water into water vapor.
tutor.why_prompt: What do you notice happening to a outdoor puddle on a hot sunny day?

The liquid water changes into an invisible gas called water vapor.

review.note: Corrects the reversed direction, then introduces a container or puddle, sunlight, heat and invisibility. The follow-up requires an outside observation.

tutor.message: Evaporation and condensation move water between liquid and gas states in opposite directions! Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapor. Condensation turns water vapor back into liquid water droplets.
tutor.why_prompt: Can you share a real-world example where you have seen condensation or evaporation happen?
explanation_steps: Evaporation direction: Liquid water changes into water vapor (gas).
Condensation direction: Water vapor (gas) changes into liquid water droplets.
They are opposite physical processes in the water cycle.

review.note: Explains both directions and their relationship. Its request for a personal example relies on experience beyond the lesson, without asserting a new fact.
